ana: Heads-up — noticed a perf regression on the paged-attn path after the kernel selector change. SM90 machines are picking the Triton FlashVariant by default and throughput is worse for long-seq workloads.

miguel: Ugh. Which configs / seq len?

ana: Repro is with gpt2-style model, seq=4096, batch=4. Baseline (before selector tweak) was ~1.2k tok/s on SM90. After selector change we see ~900 tok/s.

li: Are you sure it's selector logic and not a driver/CUDA mismatch? SM90 got CUDA 12.4 on the canaries, SM80 on prod nodes still at 12.1.

ana: I ran isolated perf on the same AMI:

```
# profiling command
./bin/profile_attn --model=gpt2-xl --seq=4096 --batch=4 --list-kernels
```

ana: Output summary (hand-typed):
```
SM90: triton_flashx 1200 tok/s, cuda_flash 980 tok/s, paged_hybrid(triton) 900 tok/s
SM80: triton_flashx 800 tok/s, cuda_flash 1150 tok/s, paged_hybrid(cuda) 1150 tok/s
```

ana: So on SM90 Triton kernel is slower for paged/hybrid than native CUDA kernel. Selector picked triton by heuristic weight=0.7.

sam: Interesting flip. That suggests kernel implementation has different perf cliff on SM90. Could be kernel launch overhead or register pressure for larger SM.

miguel: Any NVPROF traces or Nsight?

ana: Collected simple nvprof-ish counters (warp execution efficiency, achieved occupancy). Traces show higher register spill and lower achieved occupancy for the Triton variant on SM90 with 4096 window.

li: Maybe Triton is emitting a tile size that maps poorly to SM90's new register file layout. We saw similar with flashpaged earlier.

ana: Quick patch suggestion: tune selector to prefer CUDA variant for paged_hybrid when seq >= 2048 or when arch==sm90 and cuda_version < 12.5 (we observed driver sensitivity).

miguel: Could also add a runtime microbenchmark: when a new node joins, run a 1-minute kernel probe for common seq lengths and cache the per-arch best kernel. Avoid global heuristics.

sam: That has higher safety but adds startup jitter. Maybe run it in background and use previous cached choice until probe finishes.

ana: Also KV cache behavior: on SM90 we saw a spike in memory fragmentation causing slightly higher GC for large KV caches when Triton chosen. Might be combined effect.

li: Re batching heuristics: current dynbatch threshold tries to maximize throughput by grouping small requests, but if kernel is sensitive to seq length distribution it can cause bad kernel choice. We should make selector aware of batch composition (p50/p90 seq length) not just avg.

miguel: Agreed. Proposal: add two quick features:
- selector: per-arch kernel scores + per-seq-bucket tuning (buckets: <512, 512–2048, >2048)
- batching: prefer to split batches across seq buckets when it improves kernel compatibility (cost model to be small)

sam: For experiments, we need an AB test metric: tokens/sec as primary, p95 latency, and model-output diffs (to ensure numerical parity).

ana: I ran a small canary with modified selector (prefer cuda for >2048 on sm90) and got these results:
```
canary A (old selector): 900 tok/s, p95 1200ms
canary B (prefer cuda >2048): 1180 tok/s, p95 900ms
```

ana: That seems promising.

ops-bot: deploy canary to pool-a succeeded (id=prefetch-probe-20260316).

dev-bot: perf-check CI: runner/sm90-4096 passed basic smoke, but flaky on memory-counters (2/5). See logs: https://ci/internal/1234

li: Need to add a regression test in nightly that compares triton vs cuda kernel per-arch for seq {512,1024,2048,4096} and records token/sec. Fail if delta > 10% in either direction unexpectedly.

miguel: Also let's add metric to Console: per-kernel per-arch token/sec time-series so we can detect these flips automatically.

sam: Implementation plan:
- short-term: selector patch prefer cuda for >2048 on sm90 (PR ready, small change)
- medium: per-node probe + per-arch cached scores, batching aware of seq buckets, add regression tests
- long-term: contribute Triton kernel patches upstream to fix register pressure or adjust tile sizes for SM90.

ana: I'll open PR for the quick selector change and attach the probe harness + perf traces. Want reviewers @miguel @li.

miguel: Review incoming. Add flamegraph and nvprof excerpt in PR. :+1:

li: Also ping infra to upgrade some test pools to CUDA 12.5 to see if behavior changes.

ops-bot: infra ticket created: INFRA-2049 (upgrade-sm90-testpools).

ana: Thanks all. Going to run wider canary across two regions tomorrow morning. Will post numbers here.

sam: Nice catch. Small selector heuristics bite us again :grimacing:

ana: Yeah — selector heuristics are powerful but we need more per-arch empirical data.

miguel: Great thread. Keep logs and attach to the PR so QA can reproduce.

ana: Will do. End of thread.
